title: Soft Body Simulation Improvement | Clo 2025.1 Features Deep Dive
description:
The new update to our hardware in CLO 2025.1 allows you to apply soft body simulation not only to CLO avatars but also to non-rigged custom avatars for more realistic deformation and movement.

Check out other new features here:https://clo3d.com/en/clo/features

Questions? Comment below or ask in our CLO discord server: https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/7814962429977-How-can-I-join-CLO-Discord?utm_campaign=multi_item_banner_JointheOfficialCLODiscord&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=later-linkinbio

markdown_content: ## Softbody Simulation Overview in Clo 2025.1 This section explains the new Softbody simulation feature in Clo 2025.1, focusing on its application to avatars regardless of rigging status. It covers enabling Softbody, stiffness adjustments, and real-time simulation effects. Softbody simulation can now be applied to avatars that are not rigged or lack a skeleton, expanding beyond previous versions where rigging was required. To activate Softbody on an unrigged avatar, select the avatar or OBJ, open the Property Editor, and enable Softbody simulation. A stiffness slider allows control over the softness or rigidity of the simulated body: - Higher values increase stiffness, making the avatar less deformable. - Lower values decrease stiffness, making the avatar more plush and squishy. Once enabled, pressing "Simulate" initiates real-time physics simulation where the avatar deforms and bounces according to the stiffness setting. Changes to stiffness during simulation update the avatar’s behavior dynamically, showing immediate softbody response such as bouncing or conforming to external forces. Using the shortcut Shift + W or toggling garment display allows visualization of pattern pieces interacting with the avatar. Pushing pattern pieces against the avatar demonstrates how the softbody mesh deforms and reacts to collisions and pressure in real time. --- ## Practical Applications of Softbody Simulation This section details practical uses of Softbody simulation in garment design, specifically for adding objects like shoulder pads, bras, and backpacks. It also covers importing external OBJ files and setup considerations. Softbody simulation is useful for integrating additional soft or rigid objects into garments, such as: - Shoulder pads - Bras - Backpacks ### Importing and Preparing OBJ Files When importing external OBJ files to apply Softbody simulation: - Ensure the OBJ mesh is clean with no intersections or holes. - Mesh errors prevent proper Softbody simulation. To import: 1. Go to **File > Import > Add OBJ**. 2. Select the OBJ file. 3. Resize and position the OBJ in the 3D window as needed. 4. Simulate garment draping over the OBJ before enabling Softbody on the imported object. ### Enabling Softbody on Imported Objects Once positioned: - Select the imported OBJ. - Enable Softbody simulation in the Property Editor. - Adjust stiffness (e.g., 800 for moderate stiffness). - Begin simulation to see how the object interacts with garments and avatar. Lower stiffness values allow visible deformation when pressure is applied, with objects bouncing back naturally. --- ## Using Avatar Tape for Attachment This section explains how Softbody objects can be attached to avatars using Avatar Tape and its behavior during simulation. Avatar Tape can be used to attach Softbody objects to avatars, ensuring they move together during simulation. This is particularly useful for objects like shoulder pads or accessories that need to stay fixed relative to the avatar. To use Avatar Tape: 1. Enable Avatar Tape in the toggle menu. 2. Attach the Softbody object to the avatar using the tape. 3. Simulate the scene to observe the attached object following avatar movement and deformation. Note: While Avatar Tape works with Softbody, the regular tacking feature does not. Detachment is done by right-clicking the Avatar Tape and selecting detach, after which the object moves independently during simulation. --- ## Troubleshooting Mesh Issues for Softbody Simulation This section covers common mesh problems that prevent Softbody simulation and how to identify and fix them. Softbody simulation requires clean, manifold meshes without holes or self-intersections. If the imported OBJ has mesh issues: - A warning appears indicating open holes or self-intersections. - Additional warnings specify the types of mesh problems detected. To diagnose: 1. Use the toggle menu to enable **Show Wireframe**. 2. Visually inspect the mesh for holes and intersecting geometry. Mesh errors must be corrected in external 3D modeling software before re-importing. Only clean meshes will support stable Softbody simulation. --- # Summary Clo 2025.1 enhances Softbody simulation by enabling it on unrigged avatars and imported OBJ objects, with adjustable stiffness and real-time feedback. Practical applications include integrating shoulder pads and accessories with dynamic deformation. Avatar Tape supports attachment of Softbody objects to avatars for synchronized motion. Mesh integrity is crucial; holes and intersections must be fixed to avoid simulation errors.
